title: United Arab Emirates
capsule: The United Arab Emirates was formed on 2 December 1971 when six of the seven Trucial States — Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm al-Quwain, and Fujairah — joined in a federation upon British withdrawal from the Persian Gulf; Ras al-Khaimah acceded in February 1972. Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan of Abu Dhabi served as president from founding until his death in 2004, presiding over the transformation of the federation from a largely agricultural and pearling economy into a major oil-exporting and financial hub. Abu Dhabi holds the majority of the federation's petroleum reserves, while Dubai developed as a global trade and tourism centre. The UAE has maintained political stability under a federal monarchy, with the presidency remaining with the Al Nahyan family of Abu Dhabi.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The UAE's internationally recognised borders are well defined by treaty, though the boundary with Oman includes several enclaves and exclaves whose precise delimitation has been disputed; the dataset polygon reflects broadly accepted limits.
